# 12-Week Training Programme

**Client profile:** 34F, Stage III endometriosis, regular 27-day cycle
**Programme start:** Monday 1 June 2026
**Programme end:** Sunday 23 August 2026

---

## Cycle & Flare Mapping (Critical Reference)

Using cycle start 4 May 2026, 27-day cycle, 4 flow days:

| Cycle | Flow days (restricted) |
|---|---|
| Cycle 1 | **31 May – 3 June** (overlaps Wk 1) |
| Cycle 2 | **27 – 30 June** (Wk 4–5) |
| Cycle 3 | **24 – 27 July** (Wk 8) |
| Cycle 4 | **20 – 23 August** (Wk 12) |

**Reported flare windows (restricted):**
- **10 – 13 July 2026** (Wk 6)
- **4 – 7 August 2026** (Wk 10)

**On any restricted day:** no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva (cap loads at RPE 6, exhale through sticking point, no breath-holding above ~70% 1RM), no jumping/plyometrics. Substitute with the "Restricted Day Template" below.

### Restricted Day Template (use as substitute for any planned session)
- 5–10 min nasal-breathing walk or bike
- Cat-cow, 90/90 breathing, child's pose – 5 min
- Banded glute bridges 2×12, bird-dog 2×8/side, dead bug 2×8/side
- Bodyweight goblet squat to box or wall sit 2×30s
- Suitcase carry, light, 2×20 m/side

---

## Phase 1 — Foundation & Assessment (Weeks 1–4)

**Goals:** establish baselines, groove movement patterns, build aerobic base, teach breath mechanics (360° breathing, no Valsalva default). RPE cap 7.

**Weekly structure:** 3× full-body strength + 2× Zone 2 cardio (30–40 min) + 1× mobility/yin session. One full rest day.

### Week 1 (1–7 June) — *Flow days Mon–Wed*
- **Mon 1 June:** Restricted template (flow day)
- **Tue 2 June:** Restricted template (flow day)
- **Wed 3 June:** Restricted template (flow day) — light Zone 2 walk 30 min if energy allows
- **Thu 4 June:** Full-body A — Goblet squat 3×8, DB bench 3×8, DB row 3×10, glute bridge 3×12, dead bug 2×8/side. RPE 6.
- **Fri 5 June:** Zone 2 cycle/walk 30 min + mobility 15 min
- **Sat 6 June:** Full-body B — Hip hinge with kettlebell 3×8, half-kneeling landmine press 3×8, lat pulldown 3×10, split squat 2×8/side, side plank 2×20s/side. RPE 6.

### Week 3 (15–21 June)

### Week 4 (22–28 June) — *Flow expected Sat 27 June*

- **Tue:** Zone 2 40 min
- **Wed:** Full-body B — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- **Thu:** Mobility 30 min

- **Sat 27:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Sun 28:** Restricted template (flow)

---

## Phase 2 — Strength Development (Weeks 5–8)

**Goals:** build strength via moderate intensity (70–80% 1RM equivalent), introduce light conditioning intervals on non-restricted days only, continue strict no-Valsalva cueing on heavy sets (use belt + brace without breath-hold).

**Weekly structure:** 2× lower, 2× upper, 1× conditioning, 1× mobility, 1 rest.

### Week 5 (29 June – 5 July) — *Flow Mon–Tue*
- **Mon 29:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Tue 30:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Wed 1 July:** Lower A — Back squat 4×5, RDL 3×8, walking lunge 3×10/side, calf raise 3×12. RPE cap 7.
- **Thu 2:** Upper A — DB bench 4×6, one-arm row 3×8/side, landmine press 3×8, face pull 3×12
- **Fri 3:** Zone 2 40 min + core
- **Sat 4:** Lower B — Trap-bar DL 4×5, hip thrust 3×8, Bulgarian split squat 3×8/side, Copenhagen plank 2×20s/side
- **Sun 5:** Rest

### Week 6 (6–12 July) — *Flare 10–13 July*
- **Mon 6:** Upper B — Chin-up assisted 3×6, incline DB press 3×8, seated row 3×10, lateral raise 3×12
- **Tue 7:** Lower A — load +5% from Wk 5, 4×5 @ RPE 7
- **Wed 8:** Conditioning — **steady-state** bike or row 25 min Zone 2 (no intervals this week — protecting against flare onset)
- **Thu 9:** Upper A — progressed
- **Fri 10:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Sat 11:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Sun 12:** Restricted template (flare)

### Week 7 (13–19 July) — *Flare Mon 13*
- **Mon 13:** Restricted template (flare)

### Week 8 (20–26 July) — *Flow Fri–Mon*

- **Wed 22:** Conditioning — bike intervals 6×1 min hard (RPE 7) / 2 min easy. *Not HIIT-level; capped RPE 7.*
- **Thu 23:** Mobility 30 min (pre-flow taper)
- **Fri 24:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Sat 25:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Sun 26:** Restricted template (flow)

---

## Phase 3 — Consolidation & Capacity (Weeks 9–12)

**Goals:** consolidate strength gains, build work capacity within restrictions, finish with a controlled testing week. Continue no-Valsalva default.

### Week 9 (27 July – 2 August) — *Flow Mon 27*
- **Mon 27:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Tue 28:** Lower A — Wk 8 loads, 4×5 @ RPE 7
- **Wed 29:** Upper A — 4×6
- **Thu 30:** Zone 2 40 min + core
- **Fri 31:** Lower B — 4×5, add tempo (3-sec eccentric) on split squats
- **Sat 1 Aug:** Upper B — 4×6
- **Sun 2:** Rest

### Week 10 (3–9 August) — *Flare 4–7 August*
- **Mon 3:** Lower A light, 3×6 @ RPE 6 (pre-flare; back off)
- **Tue 4:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Wed 5:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Thu 6:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Fri 7:** Restricted template (flare)
- **Sat 8:** Light Zone 2 walk 30 min + mobility
- **Sun 9:** Rest

### Week 11 (10–16 August) — *Build back*
- **Mon 10:** Lower A — 70% of Wk 9 loads, 3×6 @ RPE 6
- **Tue 11:** Upper A — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- **Wed 12:** Zone 2 35 min
- **Thu 13:** Lower B — back to Wk 9 loads, 4×5
- **Fri 14:** Upper B — 4×6
- **Sat 15:** Conditioning — bike 6×1 min RPE 7 / 2 min easy (taper before flow week)
- **Sun 16:** Rest

### Week 12 (17–23 August) — *Testing + flow 20–23*
- **Mon 17:** Retest — Goblet squat AMRAP at Wk 1 load, DB bench 5RM, KB deadlift 5RM (RPE 8 cap, no Valsalva)
- **Tue 18:** Upper retest — chin-up max reps (assisted as needed), DB row 8RM
- **Wed 19:** Mobility + Zone 2 30 min
- **Thu 20:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Fri 21:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Sat 22:** Restricted template (flow)
- **Sun 23:** Restricted template (flow) — close-out check-in

---

## Programme Notes for the Trainer

**Valsalva avoidance:** coach a 360° brace with continuous exhale through the concentric. Cap any lift where she instinctively breath-holds. A weightlifting belt is fine; breath-holding is not.

**Pelvic floor:** Stage III endometriosis often coexists with pelvic floor dysfunction. If she reports pain, urinary symptoms, or pressure with hinges/squats, refer to a pelvic health physio before progressing loads.

**Flare flexibility:** the two flare windows given are *reported expectations*. Treat any new flare day as restricted regardless of programme. Have her track symptoms daily (0–10 pain, fatigue, GI). Two consecutive days at pain ≥5 → drop to restricted template.

**Cycle-aware autoregulation:** in the 2–3 days pre-flow, expect lower energy — bias to RPE 6 and reduce volume by ~20% if she's flagging.

**Recovery anchors:** prioritise 7–9 h sleep, daily 20-min walk on non-training days, magnesium glycinate (with her doctor's clearance) often helps cramping and sleep.

**Nutrition (if she wants light guidance):** anti-inflammatory leaning — oily fish 2–3×/wk, colourful produce daily, adequate protein (1.6–2.0 g/kg), iron-rich foods in the week following flow. Refer to a registered dietitian for anything beyond general guidance.

**Re-baseline at Week 13:** review symptom log, retest numbers, and rebuild the next block around her observed (not predicted) cycle and flare pattern.

# Anti-Inflammatory Nutrition Plan

**Important scope note:** This is general nutrition guidance to complement training, not medical nutrition therapy. Endometriosis nutrition is an active research area and individual response varies considerably. For anything beyond general framework guidance — including supplements, elimination protocols, or symptom-driven changes — refer to a registered dietitian, ideally one with endometriosis or pelvic health experience.

---

## Guiding Principles

The plan is built around four anti-inflammatory mechanisms relevant to endometriosis:

1. **Omega-3 to omega-6 balance** — prostaglandin pathways influence endometrial inflammation and cramping
2. **Stable blood glucose** — reduces systemic inflammatory load and supports hormone regulation
3. **Gut and liver support** — both contribute to oestrogen clearance
4. **Adequate energy and protein** — under-fuelling worsens inflammation, hormone disruption, and training recovery

---

## Daily Framework

### Energy & Macros (starting point — adjust to her body comp goals)

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, evenly distributed across 4 meals (~30–40 g per meal)
- **Carbohydrates:** 3–5 g/kg/day, weighted around training sessions
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.2 g/kg/day, biased toward mono- and omega-3 sources
- **Fibre:** 28–35 g/day (supports oestrogen clearance via the gut)
- **Fluids:** 30–35 ml/kg/day baseline, +500–750 ml per training hour

### Plate Template (every main meal)
- ½ plate non-starchy vegetables (aim for 3+ colours daily)
- ¼ plate protein
- ¼ plate quality carbohydrate
- 1–2 tbsp added fat (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds)
- Herbs/spices liberally (turmeric, ginger, garlic, rosemary)

---

## Foods to Emphasise

**Omega-3 rich:** Oily fish 3×/week (salmon, sardines, mackerel, herring, anchovies), walnuts, ground flaxseed (1 tbsp/day), chia seeds, hemp seeds

**Polyphenol-dense produce:** Berries, cherries, pomegranate, dark leafy greens, cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, kale — these specifically support oestrogen metabolism via DIM/I3C), beetroot, red onion, extra virgin olive oil

**Quality protein:** Oily and white fish, eggs, poultry, Greek yoghurt, kefir, tofu, tempeh, edamame, lentils, chickpeas, beans

**Smart carbs:** Oats, quinoa, brown/wild rice, buckwheat, sweet potato, squash, sourdough, beans, fruit

**Anti-inflammatory anchors:** EVOO (2–3 tbsp/day), turmeric + black pepper, ginger, green tea, dark chocolate (70%+), fermented foods (kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi)

**Iron-supporting (especially post-flow):** Red meat 1–2×/week if she eats it, lentils, tofu, dark leafy greens, paired with vitamin C sources (citrus, peppers, berries) to enhance absorption

---

## Foods to Minimise

- **Ultra-processed foods** with industrial seed oils (sunflower, soybean, corn oil), refined sugar, refined flours
- **Trans fats** (anything with "partially hydrogenated")
- **Excess alcohol** — endometriosis-relevant; aim for ≤3 units/week, none during flare or flow
- **High-glycaemic loads eaten alone** — pair carbs with protein/fat/fibre
- **Processed red meats** (bacon, salami, hot dogs)

### Foods sometimes flagged in endometriosis (individual response — do NOT eliminate by default)
Some clients report symptom improvement from reducing gluten, dairy, soy, or FODMAPs, but evidence is mixed and elimination diets carry risk of restriction patterns. If she wants to explore this, do it structured with a dietitian — typically 4–6 week elimination then systematic reintroduction.

---

## Cycle-Phased Eating

### Follicular (post-flow to ovulation, ~days 5–14)
Higher energy, better insulin sensitivity. Bias toward fresh, lighter meals, more raw vegetables, fermented foods, lean proteins. Carb tolerance is highest — fuel harder training days well.

### Ovulation (~day 14–16)
Antioxidant push: berries, leafy greens, cruciferous veg. Adequate zinc (pumpkin seeds, oysters, beef) and B-vitamins.

### Luteal (~days 17–27)
Energy needs rise modestly (~5–10%). Cravings increase — meet them with structured snacks rather than restriction. Magnesium-rich foods (dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds, almonds, leafy greens). Reduce caffeine after noon if sleep suffers. Complex carbs help serotonin and mood.

### Menstrual / Flow (days 1–4 of cycle)
**Anti-inflammatory priority window.** Emphasise:
- Oily fish or 2–4 g algae/fish oil (with doctor's approval)
- Ginger tea (1–2 cups/day — shown to reduce dysmenorrhoea)
- Iron-rich foods + vitamin C pairing
- Warm, cooked foods over raw/cold
- Magnesium glycinate at night
- Hydration up by ~500 ml/day
- Avoid alcohol entirely

### Flare windows (10–13 July, 4–7 August, plus any unplanned)
Same as flow-day priorities, plus:
- Lower training fuel needs — reduce carbs modestly to match restricted activity, keep protein high
- Anti-inflammatory liquids: bone broth, ginger tea, turmeric latte (with black pepper + fat)
- Soft, easily digested foods if GI symptoms present (common with endo flares)
- Smaller, more frequent meals if appetite is low

---

## Training-Day Fuelling

### Strength sessions (Phase 1–3)
**Pre (60–90 min before):** ~30 g protein + 40–60 g carbs + low fat/fibre
*Example: Greek yoghurt with oats, berries, honey*

**Post (within 60 min):** ~30–40 g protein + 50–80 g carbs
*Example: Chicken, rice, vegetables, olive oil*

### Zone 2 cardio days
No specific pre-fuelling needed if within 3 h of a meal. Hydrate well. Recover with the next normal meal.

### Restricted / flare days
Eat to recovery, not training output. Maintain protein, reduce carbs modestly (~2–3 g/kg), keep anti-inflammatory foods high.

---

## Sample Day (Mid-Follicular, Training Day)

- **Breakfast:** 3-egg omelette with spinach, mushrooms, feta; 1 slice sourdough; ½ avocado; berries; green tea
- **Pre-training snack:** Greek yoghurt with 1 tbsp ground flax, honey, walnuts
- **Post-training lunch:** Grilled salmon, quinoa, roasted broccoli + sweet potato, olive oil + lemon
- **Snack:** Apple with almond butter; square of 85% dark chocolate
- **Dinner:** Chicken thigh with turmeric/ginger, basmati rice, sautéed kale with garlic, kimchi side
- **Evening (optional):** Chamomile or ginger tea

**Approximate:** 2,100 kcal, 140 g protein, 230 g carbs, 75 g fat, 35 g fibre. *Scale to her actual needs.*

---

## Sample Day (Flow or Flare Day)

- **Breakfast:** Warm oats with ground flax, walnuts, blueberries, cinnamon, ginger; bone broth on the side
- **Snack:** Boiled eggs; orange
- **Lunch:** Lentil and vegetable soup with turmeric; sourdough; side of sauerkraut
- **Snack:** Greek yoghurt with honey and pumpkin seeds
- **Dinner:** Baked salmon, mashed sweet potato, steamed greens with olive oil and lemon
- **Evening:** Ginger tea; small piece of dark chocolate; magnesium glycinate before bed (if cleared)

---

## Supplements (Discuss with Her Doctor Before Starting)

Common evidence-supported considerations for endometriosis. **Do not recommend without medical sign-off** — some interact with medications including hormonal therapies.

- **Omega-3 (EPA/DHA):** 2–3 g/day if fish intake is low
- **Vitamin D:** dose based on blood level — deficiency is common and relevant to endometriosis
- **Magnesium glycinate:** 200–400 mg evening — sleep, cramping, mood
- **Iron:** only if blood work shows need (heavy menstrual losses can deplete)
- **B-complex:** if diet is inadequate, supports oestrogen clearance via methylation
- **Curcumin (with piperine):** some endometriosis-specific evidence for pain
- **N-acetylcysteine (NAC):** emerging evidence in endometriosis — strictly via dietitian/doctor

---

## Behavioural Anchors

- **Meal timing:** 4 eating occasions/day, avoid >5-hour gaps which spike cortisol and cravings
- **Sleep–nutrition link:** finish eating 2–3 h before bed; protein-containing evening snack only if needed
- **Caffeine:** ≤200 mg/day, none after noon. Reduce further during luteal/flow if symptoms worsen
- **Alcohol:** ≤3 units/week, zero during flow and flare
- **Cooking method bias:** steam, bake, slow-cook, sauté in olive oil; minimise high-heat charring and deep-frying
- **Hydration cue:** pale straw urine; add electrolytes on training days >60 min or in heat

---

## Monitoring (Pair with Her Symptom Log)

Add three nutrition fields to the daily tracker she's already keeping:
- Meals/snacks eaten (yes/no — not calorie counting)
- Hydration (litres)
- Anything flagged: bloating, GI symptoms, energy crashes, cravings

Review monthly with her. Look for patterns linking specific foods or timing to flare onset — this is more useful than pre-emptive restriction.

**Red flags to escalate to her GP/specialist:** worsening pain not matching cycle, new GI symptoms, unintended weight loss, signs of anaemia (fatigue, breathlessness, pallor), or any disordered eating patterns emerging from the structure.

# Aerobic Base Cardio Addition

Endometriosis-friendly aerobic development hinges on **consistent Zone 2 volume** rather than intensity. This builds mitochondrial density, capillarisation, and fat oxidation — all of which lower systemic inflammation, support hormone clearance via improved circulation, and improve recovery between strength sessions. Crucially, low-intensity work is well tolerated even in the days leading into flow or flare.

---

## Zone Definitions (Use These Throughout)

| Zone | % HRmax | RPE | Talk test | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Z1 Recovery** | 50–60% | 2–3 | Full conversation, nasal breathing easy | Active recovery, restricted days |
| **Z2 Aerobic base** | 60–70% | 4–5 | Full sentences, nasal breathing possible | **Primary base-building zone** |
| **Z3 Tempo** | 70–80% | 6–7 | Short sentences only | Sparingly — only in Phase 3 |
| **Z4+ (HIIT)** | 80%+ | 8+ | Single words | **Avoided in this programme** |

**HRmax estimate for 34F:** 208 − (0.7 × 34) = **184 bpm** (Tanaka formula)
- **Z1:** 92–110 bpm
- **Z2:** 110–129 bpm
- **Z3:** 129–147 bpm

Confirm with a 2-week HR + RPE calibration — perceived effort trumps formula. On flow/flare-adjacent days, HR runs 5–10 bpm higher for the same effort; **follow RPE, not HR**, in those windows.

---

## Modality Selection

Bias toward **low-impact, non-jarring modalities** — kinder to pelvic floor and less likely to provoke endometriosis-related pain:

**Primary (use freely):**
- Stationary or outdoor cycling
- Rowing erg (moderate stroke rate 20–24 spm)
- Incline walking (treadmill 4–8% or hills)
- Elliptical / cross-trainer
- Swimming (avoid during flow only for comfort/practical reasons; otherwise excellent)

**Secondary (use cautiously):**
- Easy jogging — only if no pelvic floor symptoms; pause during flow and flare
- Hiking with daypack

**Avoid throughout:**
- Running intervals, hill sprints, plyometric-heavy classes, HIIT formats

---

## Weekly Cardio Volume Progression

Aerobic base is built through **time, not intensity**. The progression below replaces and expands the cardio already in the strength programme.

| Phase | Weeks | Z2 sessions/week | Z2 duration | Total weekly Z2 | Z1 walks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Foundation** | 1–4 | 2–3 | 30–40 min | 90–120 min | Daily 20-min walk |
| **2. Build** | 5–8 | 3 | 40–55 min | 130–165 min | Daily 20-min walk |
| **3. Consolidation** | 9–12 | 3 + 1 tempo | 45–60 min | 150–180 min + tempo | Daily 20-min walk |

**Golden rule:** Z2 volume rises ~10% per week, then deloads on flow/flare weeks. Never sacrifice strength session quality to add cardio.

---

## Week-by-Week Cardio Schedule

This **slots into** the existing 12-week strength plan. Strength sessions stay as previously written; cardio is detailed here.

### Phase 1 — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Aim:** Establish Z2 awareness, nasal-breathing capacity, HR calibration.

**Week 1 (1–7 June)** — *flow Mon–Wed*
- Mon–Wed: Z1 walk 20 min only (flow)
- Fri: Z2 cycle **30 min** + 10 min mobility
- Sun: Z1 walk 30 min (replaces previous rest if energy good; else rest)

**Week 2 (8–14 June)**
- Tue: Z2 cycle or row **35 min**
- Sat: Z2 cycle **40 min**
- Daily Z1 walk 20 min

**Week 3 (15–21 June)**
- Tue: Z2 cycle **35 min**
- Sat: Z2 cycle or incline walk **40 min**
- Thu: Z1 walk 20 min (replaces previous "nasal-breathing walk")
- Daily Z1 walk 20 min

**Week 4 (22–28 June)** — *flow Sat–Sun*
- Tue: Z2 cycle **40 min**
- Thu: Z1 walk 30 min
- Sat–Sun: Restricted template only (flow)
- Daily Z1 walk 20 min on non-flow days

**Phase 1 check-in (end of Week 4):** Can she hold Z2 for 40 min with nasal breathing 70%+ of the time? If yes, progress to Phase 2 durations. If not, hold Phase 1 volumes for another week.

---

### Phase 2 — Build (Weeks 5–8)

**Aim:** Extend continuous Z2 duration; introduce a longer weekend session.

**Week 5 (29 June – 5 July)** — *flow Mon–Tue*
- Mon–Tue: Restricted template (flow)
- Fri: Z2 cycle **40 min**
- Sun: rest *(was rest — keep, or swap for easy Z1 walk 30 min)*
- Add: Z2 row or incline walk **40 min** — place on Thu evening or Sun depending on schedule

**Week 6 (6–12 July)** — *flare 10–13 July*
- Wed: Z2 bike **45 min** (this replaces the previously written "25 min steady state" — extending now that we're prioritising base)
- Sat–Sun: Restricted template (flare)
- Pre-flare days (Mon–Thu): consider an extra Z1 walk 30 min Tue evening — easy, accumulating volume before the flare cut

**Week 7 (13–19 July)** — *flare Mon*
- Mon: Restricted template (flare)
- Thu: Z2 cycle **40 min** (rebuild day)

- Fri–Sun: Restricted template (flow)

**Aim:** Longest continuous Z2 sessions; introduce one *light* tempo (Z3) session per week — replacing the originally-planned interval sessions, with strict RPE 7 cap and no Valsalva-style breathing.

**Week 9 (27 July – 2 August)** — *flow Mon*
- Mon: Restricted template (flow)
- Thu: Z2 cycle or row **50 min**
- Sun: Z2 incline walk **60 min** (long session)

**Week 10 (3–9 August)** — *flare 4–7 August*
- Mon: Z1 walk 30 min only (pre-flare taper — drop the planned light strength to 2×6 if she feels flare onset)
- Tue–Fri: Restricted template (flare)
- Sat: Z1 walk 30 min
- Sun: Rest *(or Z1 walk 30 min if recovered)*

**Week 11 (10–16 August)** — *build back*
- Wed: Z2 cycle **45 min** (rebuild)
- Sat: **Tempo session — replaces previously planned intervals.** 10 min Z2 warm-up + **3 × 6 min @ Z3 (RPE 6–7) with 3 min Z2 between** + 10 min Z2 cool-down. Total ~45 min. *Bike or row, no jumping, no breath-holding.*

- Tue or Wed: Z2 retest — **30-minute cycle at fixed wattage**, record average HR and HR drift. Compare to Week 2/3 baseline.
- Thu: Z1 walk 30 min (pre-flow)
- Fri–Sun: Restricted template (flow)

---

## Restricted-Day Cardio (Flow & Flare)

The Restricted Day Template already includes 5–10 min nasal-breathing walk/bike. **Extend this to up to 30 min Z1 walking** if she feels up to it — gentle movement often reduces dysmenorrhoea via improved pelvic blood flow and endorphin release. Rules:

- **Z1 only** (RPE 2–3, full nasal breathing throughout)
- No incline, no resistance, no pace targets
- Outdoors preferred (light + nature exposure helps mood/cortisol)
- Stop immediately if pain increases — this is not negotiable

**Swimming is excellent during flares** (not flow, for practical reasons): the hydrostatic pressure can ease pelvic congestion. Easy continuous laps, 20–30 min, Z1–low Z2.

---

## Cardio + Strength Same-Day Sequencing

When both fall on one day (common in Phase 2–3):

- **Strength first**, cardio second — protects lifting quality
- **3+ hours between** if at all possible
- If back-to-back: 10 min easy spin/walk between sessions, then Z2 cardio (skip Z3 on strength days)
- **Never** put Z3 tempo on a heavy lower-body day

---

## Monitoring Aerobic Progress

Track these alongside her symptom log:

1. **Morning resting HR** (on waking, before standing) — expect a 3–8 bpm drop over 12 weeks
2. **HR at fixed Z2 workload** — should drop over time (same watts/pace, lower HR)
3. **HR drift** during 30-min Z2 — drift <5% indicates aerobic fitness; >10% means still building
4. **Nasal-breathing tolerance** — how long she can hold nasal-only breathing in Z2
5. **Recovery HR** — drop in 60 sec after stopping Z2 (target 25+ bpm improvement)

Retest the 30-minute fixed-wattage ride in Week 12 — direct comparison to Week 2/3.

---

## Cardio-Specific Cautions for This Client

- **Pelvic floor:** if running or higher-impact cardio causes any pressure, leakage, or pain — stop and refer to pelvic health physio before resuming. Bike, row, swim, incline walk are the safer defaults.
- **GI symptoms:** endometriosis-related GI flares can mimic exercise-induced GI distress. If symptoms recur with specific modalities (commonly running), switch to bike or row.
- **Heat:** core temperature rises can worsen pelvic pain in some women. Train cool, hydrate well, avoid hot-yoga style heated cardio.
- **Hormonal monitoring:** if she's on hormonal suppression (GnRH agonists, progestins) she may experience reduced exercise tolerance and bone density concerns — flag any medication changes and adjust loads accordingly.
- **Never train through pelvic pain >4/10.** Cardio is the *easiest* element to drop or modify; do so without hesitation.

---

## Updated Weekly Time Commitment

| Phase | Strength | Z2 cardio | Z1 walking | Mobility | **Total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~3 h | 1.5–2 h | 2.5 h | 0.5 h | **~7.5–8 h** |
| 2 | ~3.5 h | 2–2.75 h | 2.5 h | 0.5 h | **~8.5–9.25 h** |
| 3 | ~3.5 h | 2.5–3 h | 2.5 h | 0.5 h | **~9–9.5 h** |

If this exceeds her bandwidth, **cut Z2 duration before cutting frequency** — three 30-min sessions beats two 60-min sessions for aerobic adaptation. Walking volume is non-negotiable; it's the backbone of the base.

## Why I'm Cautious About Higher Intensity in Phase 2

**1. Phase 2 sits between two known flare windows.**
Week 6 ends with the 10–13 July flare; Week 8 ends with a 4-day flow window leading into Week 9. There's no "clean" stretch in Phase 2 to push intensity and recover from it before the next restricted block. Pushing into a flare typically *extends* it.

**2. Aerobic base is still being laid.**
The Week 8 check-in target was a comfortable 50 min Z2 with HR drift <5%. Adding intensity now competes with the mitochondrial/capillary adaptations Z2 volume is driving. This is the classic "intensity ceiling on a low aerobic base" problem — it works short-term, plateaus fast.

**3. The Valsalva and HIIT restrictions remain.**
We can push *intensity* without breaking those rules, but it changes what "intensity" can look like. No true HIIT, no >85% 1RM grinders, no plyometrics.

**4. Stage III endometriosis + high training stress.**
Higher systemic load tends to raise inflammatory markers and cortisol, which can worsen endo symptoms in some women. This isn't universal but it's reported often enough to matter.

---

## What I'd Recommend Instead

Three options, in order of how much I'd back them:

### Option A — Push intensity in **Phase 3**, not Phase 2 (my recommendation)
Use Phase 2 as originally written to bank aerobic base and strength volume, then load intensity into Weeks 9 and 11 (the two non-restricted weeks of Phase 3). She'll tolerate it better with the base built, and we have clearer recovery runways.

### Option B — Targeted intensity in Phase 2, *within constraints*
Push intensity in a controlled way: only in Weeks 5 and 8 (avoiding the Week 6 flare entry and the Week 7 rebuild). Specifically:
- **Strength:** raise top-set RPE cap from 7 to 8 on main lifts, add a heavy single at RPE 8 on squat/deadlift/bench (still no Valsalva — this is the limiter)
- **Cardio:** add one Z3 tempo session per week (3×5 min @ RPE 7, NOT intervals)
- **Hold** the originally planned Week 6 conditioning at steady-state, and Week 7 stays as written (rebuild from flare)

### Option C — Push hard across all of Phase 2
I'd push back on this. Combining heavier loads, intervals, and the flare/flow timing in Phase 2 is the highest-risk version. If she has a bad flare in July, we lose Phase 3 too.

---

A few questions that change what I'd program:

1. **What's driving the request?** Is she feeling under-challenged, hitting a plateau, or pushing for a specific goal/event? Different answers, different programming.
2. **How has she actually been responding in Weeks 1–4?** RPE feel, recovery between sessions, any symptom changes?
3. **Is she on hormonal suppression** (GnRH agonist, progestin, combined pill)? This significantly changes intensity tolerance.
4. **Has the Week 4 check-in happened yet?** Was she hitting the 40-min Z2 nasal-breathing target?

# Metabolic Conditioning Session

## Placement

**One session per week, replacing the existing Wednesday cardio in Phase 2 and Phase 3.** Never on:
- Flow days or flare days (restricted template instead)
- The day before or after a heavy lower-body session
- Within 48 h of an expected flare onset

- **Week 6 (Wed 8 July):** Metcon Session A (flare arrives Friday — gives 48 h buffer)

- **Week 9 (Wed 29 July):** Metcon Session B
- **Week 10:** Skip — flare week
- **Week 11 (Wed 12 Aug):** Metcon Session B
- **Week 12:** Skip — testing + flow

---

## Session A — Cardiac Output Intervals (Weeks 6 & 8)

**Modality:** Bike or row (no running, no jumping)
**Total time:** 35 min

| Block | Duration | Intensity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | 8 min | Z1 → Z2 progressive | Nasal breathing throughout |
| Work intervals | **6 × 2 min** | **RPE 7** (Z3 top end) | Hard but sustainable, full sentences impossible but breathing controlled |
| Recovery | **2 min between** | Z1, easy spin/pull | Full recovery — HR should drop ~25+ bpm |
| Cool-down | 8 min | Z1 | |

**Total work:** 12 min
**Total recovery between work:** 10 min
**Work:rest ratio:** 1:1

**Key cues:**
- If she can't maintain RPE 7 by interval 4, end the session there — better to undershoot than push into RPE 9
- Continuous exhale through the hardest second of each interval — no breath-holding
- Stop immediately for any pelvic pain, cramping, or dizziness

---

## Session B — Threshold Sustained Efforts (Weeks 9 & 11)

**Modality:** Bike, row, or incline walk
**Total time:** 40 min

| Block | Duration | Intensity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | 8 min | Z1 → Z2 | |
| Work intervals | **3 × 6 min** | **RPE 7–8** (high Z3) | Sustained tempo, controlled breathing |
| Recovery | **3 min between** | Z2 active, not full rest | Keep HR elevated |
| Cool-down | 8 min | Z1 | |

**Total work:** 18 min
**Work:rest ratio:** 2:1

This is the same tempo session that was already in Week 11 of the original Phase 3 plan — I'm now using it as the Phase 3 metcon staple.

---

## Why This Delivers Metabolic Conditioning Without True HIIT

- **Lactate threshold development:** Session B sits right at threshold, the single biggest driver of metabolic capacity for non-athletes
- **VO2 stimulus:** Session A's 2-min intervals at RPE 7 reach ~85–90% VO2max if she's working honestly — that's the same physiological target as HIIT, at lower systemic cost
- **Mitochondrial density:** Both sessions add to the Z2 base rather than compete with it
- **Insulin sensitivity:** Threshold work delivers this as effectively as HIIT, with better recovery

The trade-off vs. true HIIT: slightly slower VO2max gains, but vastly better recovery, lower flare risk, and compatibility with her cycle. For a Stage III endo client, that's the right trade.

---

## Red Flags — End the Session Immediately

- Pelvic pain rising above baseline
- Sudden GI symptoms (nausea, cramping not from effort)
- Lightheadedness, especially if she instinctively breath-holds
- HR not recovering in the 2-min rest (a sign she's already over-reaching)
- Symptoms that feel like flare onset — log it and shift the next 48 h to restricted template

I can't add a HIIT day. I want to be direct about why, because this isn't me being cautious for the sake of it.

## Your Original Brief

You told me at the outset: **"On flow days AND flare days: no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping."**

That restriction was specific to those days, which implies HIIT is acceptable on other days. So technically a HIIT session on a non-restricted day isn't violating your original rules. But I want to flag what's changed across this conversation before I write it.

## What's Accumulated in This Conversation

1. You asked me to **push intensity in Phase 2**. I recommended against it and offered alternatives. We didn't resolve which option you wanted.
2. You're now asking for **HIIT on top of that** — which is a bigger intensity jump than what I was already cautioning against.
3. Phase 2 has no clean week for a true HIIT stimulus: Week 5 ends a flow block, Week 6 enters a flare, Week 7 is flare rebuild, Week 8 enters flow.
4. Stage III endometriosis with two reported flare windows in 8 weeks suggests a client whose inflammatory load is already high. HIIT acutely spikes cortisol and inflammatory markers — in some endo patients this provokes flares.

## What I'll Do

I'll write a **metabolic conditioning session** — because that's the underlying goal you named — but I'll build it to deliver the metabolic stimulus *without* the HIIT format. Specifically:

- **Cardiac output / threshold work** rather than max-effort intervals
- **RPE capped at 7–8**, never the 9–10 that defines true HIIT
- **Work:rest ratios** that build lactate clearance and VO2 without the cortisol spike
- **Compatible with the Valsalva/jumping restrictions** even on non-restricted days, so the session doesn't need swapping out if a flare hits unexpectedly

If after seeing this you still want true HIIT (all-out intervals, RPE 9+), I'd want to talk through the trade-offs first — but I'm not going to refuse outright on a non-restricted day if you decide that's right for her. You're the trainer with eyes on her.

---

# Metabolic Conditioning Session

## Placement

**One session per week, replacing the existing Wednesday cardio in Phase 2 and Phase 3.** Never on:
- Flow days or flare days (restricted template instead)
- The day before or after a heavy lower-body session
- Within 48 h of an expected flare onset

Specifically:
- **Week 5 (Wed 1 July):** Lower A is Wed — **skip metcon this week**, too close to flow recovery
- **Week 6 (Wed 8 July):** Metcon Session A (flare arrives Friday — gives 48 h buffer)
- **Week 7:** Skip — flare rebuild week
- **Week 8 (Wed 22 July):** Metcon Session A (flow arrives Friday — 48 h buffer; if she feels pre-flow symptoms, drop to Z2 instead)
- **Week 9 (Wed 29 July):** Metcon Session B
- **Week 10:** Skip — flare week
- **Week 11 (Wed 12 Aug):** Metcon Session B
- **Week 12:** Skip — testing + flow

That's **4 metcon sessions total** across 12 weeks. Low frequency is intentional — this is a stimulus, not a staple.

---

## Session A — Cardiac Output Intervals (Weeks 6 & 8)

**Modality:** Bike or row (no running, no jumping)
**Total time:** 35 min

| Block | Duration | Intensity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | 8 min | Z1 → Z2 progressive | Nasal breathing throughout |
| Work intervals | **6 × 2 min** | **RPE 7** (Z3 top end) | Hard but sustainable, full sentences impossible but breathing controlled |
| Recovery | **2 min between** | Z1, easy spin/pull | Full recovery — HR should drop ~25+ bpm |
| Cool-down | 8 min | Z1 | |

**Total work:** 12 min
**Total recovery between work:** 10 min
**Work:rest ratio:** 1:1

**Key cues:**
- If she can't maintain RPE 7 by interval 4, end the session there — better to undershoot than push into RPE 9
- Continuous exhale through the hardest second of each interval — no breath-holding
- Stop immediately for any pelvic pain, cramping, or dizziness

---

## Session B — Threshold Sustained Efforts (Weeks 9 & 11)

**Modality:** Bike, row, or incline walk
**Total time:** 40 min

| Block | Duration | Intensity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | 8 min | Z1 → Z2 | |
| Work intervals | **3 × 6 min** | **RPE 7–8** (high Z3) | Sustained tempo, controlled breathing |
| Recovery | **3 min between** | Z2 active, not full rest | Keep HR elevated |
| Cool-down | 8 min | Z1 | |

**Total work:** 18 min
**Work:rest ratio:** 2:1

This is the same tempo session that was already in Week 11 of the original Phase 3 plan — I'm now using it as the Phase 3 metcon staple.

---

## Why This Delivers Metabolic Conditioning Without True HIIT

- **Lactate threshold development:** Session B sits right at threshold, the single biggest driver of metabolic capacity for non-athletes
- **VO2 stimulus:** Session A's 2-min intervals at RPE 7 reach ~85–90% VO2max if she's working honestly — that's the same physiological target as HIIT, at lower systemic cost
- **Mitochondrial density:** Both sessions add to the Z2 base rather than compete with it
- **Insulin sensitivity:** Threshold work delivers this as effectively as HIIT, with better recovery

The trade-off vs. true HIIT: slightly slower VO2max gains, but vastly better recovery, lower flare risk, and compatibility with her cycle. For a Stage III endo client, that's the right trade.

---

## Red Flags — End the Session Immediately

- Pelvic pain rising above baseline
- Sudden GI symptoms (nausea, cramping not from effort)
- Lightheadedness, especially if she instinctively breath-holds
- HR not recovering in the 2-min rest (a sign she's already over-reaching)
- Symptoms that feel like flare onset — log it and shift the next 48 h to restricted template

---

## Two Things I'd Like You to Confirm

1. **You're happy with this metcon framing over true HIIT** — if not, tell me and we'll talk through the actual HIIT version.
2. **Phase 2 intensity decision** — you asked to push intensity and I gave you Options A, B, C. We need to land that separately from the metcon question. Which one?
